specAnchors.text: know and use the relationship between refractive index, angle of incidence and angle of refraction: n = sin i / sin r

primer.text: Refraction bends a light ray when it crosses into a new material, and Snell's law turns that bending into a calculation. One ratio — the refractive index — ties the sine of the incidence angle to the sine of the refraction angle. Rearranged, it predicts how sharply a ray bends at any boundary. This lesson defines the ratio, works the equation both ways and explains why every material lands above 1.

modules.title: Snell's law
modules.opening: Draw any ray hitting a boundary and two angles matter: one on the way in, one on the way out. Snell's law says the sines of those angles keep a fixed ratio, and that ratio is the material's refractive index. Because it compares two speeds, the index is a bare number — always above 1, larger for optically denser materials, and it works for every boundary light can cross.
keyPoints: Snell's law links the refractive index to the angles of incidence and refraction: n = sin i / sin r.
The refractive index compares the speed of light in a vacuum with the slower speed of light inside the material.
The refractive index is always larger than 1, differs between materials and has no units because it is a ratio.
More optically dense materials have higher refractive indices: about 2.4 for diamond and about 1.5 for glass.

low.restatement: Snell's law says dividing the sine of the incidence angle by the sine of the refraction angle gives the refractive index, a fixed number for the material.
low.analogy: A shopping receipt: the ratio of two prices gives one fixed exchange rate, whatever amounts you trade.
low.examPointer: Quote the equation as n = sin i / sin r and name n as the refractive index — that alone often earns the first mark.

medium.restatement: The index compares the vacuum speed of light with the slower speed inside the material, so it is a ratio with no units, always greater than 1 and bigger for optically denser materials.
medium.analogy: A marathon runner versus a wader: the same crossing takes longer through the pond, and the delay factor is the index.
medium.examPointer: When a question asks why the index has no units, answer that it is one speed divided by another — a pure ratio.

glossary.definition: The ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in a material; it has no units.
The angle between the incoming ray and the normal.
The angle between the refracted ray and the normal.
Describing a medium that slows light by a large factor, giving a high refractive index.

workedExample.prompt: A ray of light enters a glass block of refractive index 1.53, making an angle of 15° with the normal before entering the block. Calculate the angle it makes with the normal after it enters the glass.
steps: List the known quantities: refractive index n = 1.53 and angle of incidence i = 15°.
Write Snell's law: n = sin i / sin r.
Rearrange for the sine of the refraction angle: sin r = sin i / n.
Apply the inverse sine function: r = sin⁻¹(0.169) = 9.7°, which rounds to 10°.
workedExample.finalAnswer: The ray travels at about 10° to the normal inside the glass block.
